claim.quote: In that time four fully contained events with at least a 10 cm track in iron have been recorded. Three of these can be definitely attributed to neutrino interactions. The fourth event can be explained by a number of possible proton decay modes.

date.note: OSTI gives only 'Jan. 1983' for the volume; month precision.

name: Mount Blanc experiment on nucleon stability

summary.plain: After about a year of running, NUSEX had recorded four fully contained events. Three were neutrino interactions; the fourth could be a proton decay in one of several modes. By 1985 it listed three nucleon-decay candidates among 31 contained events. No experiment has confirmed proton decay.
summary.technical: Four fully contained events with at least a 10 cm iron track since 1982: three attributed to neutrino interactions, one compatible with several proton-decay modes; a proton lifetime was calculated from it. The 1985 ICRC paper reports 31 fully contained events in 2.8 years, 3 of them nucleon-decay candidates. A 2004 review notes a NUSEX candidate in the p to mu+ K0 mode with an estimated background of 0.09.

title: Mount Blanc experiment on nucleon stability
why_it_matters: An early candidate event from a proton-decay detector. No first-generation experiment established nucleon decay: a 1992 review states that no experiment has observed proton decay.
